I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when using a non-Unicode email encoding:

- Added [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/utils/encoding.py#L221-L223) in [django/utils/encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/utils/encoding.py) to convert non-ASCII domain names to Punycode (`idna`).
- Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16-L19) in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/mail/utils.py) and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/mail/message.py#L255-L262) / [`sanitize_address()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/mail/message.py#L74-L108) in [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/mail/message.py) (as well as [django/core/validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/core/validators.py) and [django/utils/html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/utils/html.py)) to convert non-ASCII domains using [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x9pkxv7q/django/utils/encoding.py#L221-L223).
